newsitem.title: CHINA: China reaffirms tax on interest from foreign loans.
newsitem.headline: China reaffirms tax on interest from foreign loans.

text.p: China has reaffirmed that it still views as taxable interest on loans to foreign financial institutions in this country from offshore banks, officials and state media said on Friday.
China's State Council, or cabinet, has recently issued a directive due to questions about the collection of such tax, the Shanghai Securities News said.
"There is nothing new in it (the directive), the rules are already in effect," an official of the State Bureau of Taxation told Reuters in Beijing.
"We just want to clarify the situation because some foreign bank branches in China have started to borrow funds from overseas," he said.

The tax on interest -- which is in addition to income tax -- is usually 20 percent of the interest total but Beijing would extend a favourable rate of 10 percent to lenders in countries which have a reciprocal tax agreement with China, the official said.

Overseas banks extending loans to foreign banks or other financial institutions in China should bear the tax but since many do not have offices in the country, banks in China were asked to pay on their behalf, the official added.
China's state banks should also pay tax on interest from foreign loans, though they could enjoy tax reductions or waivers if their loans from abroad were on favourable terms.
He said this was aimed at encouraging cheap loans for Chinese companies, though he declined to give further details.
